Cohort2Trajectory

Cohort2Trajectory turns cohort intervals into patient trajectories for analysis. A target cohort defines each patient’s observation period; state cohorts define events or periods within it. When states overlap, you choose which takes priority or whether to represent their combination.

The package accepts an R data frame, a CSV file or cohorts generated in an OMOP Common Data Model database through CDMConnector. It produces fixed-length cycles or continuous intervals, with explicit rules for state selection, allowed transitions, gaps and absorbing states. Study settings can be reused with fresh data at another site.

A small example

This example needs no database. In local input, "0" identifies the target cohort and other labels identify states. Intervals include both endpoint dates.

library(Cohort2Trajectory)

cohorts <- data.frame(
  subject_id = rep("001", 3),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "Stable", "Complication"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date("2020-01-01") + c(0, 0, 7),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date("2020-01-21")
)

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "example",
  pathToStudy = tempdir(),
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = cohorts,
  stateCohortLabels = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("Complication", "Stable"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  cycleLength = 7
)

getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)
trajectories

The patient is Stable in the first week and in Complication for the next two. The returned table also contains START and EXIT boundary rows. Input and output files are saved under file.path(tempdir(), "example").

Choosing a trajectory

A discrete trajectory selects one state per cycle. Its label describes the selection for that cycle, not necessarily every day within it. The final cycle can be shorter than cycleLength. A continuous trajectory retains selected interval dates and can resolve overlaps by priority.

You supply the clinical definitions: an episode, a history of that episode and recovery need their own cohort definitions when the analysis distinguishes them. OUT OF COHORT marks a discrete cycle with no selected state. START and EXIT mark observation boundaries.

By default, the first target interval supplies each patient’s observation period. Use targetEpisodeHandling = "All" to keep every non-overlapping target period as a separate episode, identified by episode_id. Selection and elapsed time restart in each episode; gaps between periods are omitted. Later episodes remain eligible after an absorbing state unless stopAfterAbsorbingEpisode = TRUE. See the multiple-period example.

Use mergeStates = TRUE to represent overlapping states together. mergedState() can change a combination’s destinations, absorbing status or display label. Membership is stored separately from labels.

Documentation

The documentation site contains the function reference and these guides, also available as package vignettes:

  • Getting started: local input and the three-step workflow.
  • Configure a study: observation bounds, selection and merged states.
  • Import cohort data: CSV, data frames, ATLAS and local JSON definitions.
  • Create trajectories: transition rules, gaps and saved-study reruns.
  • A weekly worked example: pneumonia history and two death states.
  • Read the output: columns, files and downstream analysis.

For CDM input, the database account needs read access to the required CDM and vocabulary tables and permission to create and drop tables in the write schema. ATLAS authentication headers can be supplied at import. Exported JSON definitions can be used without an ATLAS connection.

Reuse and analysis

A completed run saves its settings in Settings/analysisSettings.rds, including the imported cohort JSON for CDM studies. Copy that folder to rerun the study with fresh data. Keep Data private: it contains patient records.

Returned trajectories carry their cycle length, ordered state labels and absorbing states for use by TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis. Use saveRDS() to preserve both the rows and these definitions. CSV contains only the rows, so downstream tools need the definitions supplied separately. The current TMA reader accepts the default single-period format. It rejects the version-2 definition used by targetEpisodeHandling = "All"; those episodes need an analysis that preserves their separate observation boundaries.

Related packages: CohortContrast and TrajectoryViz.
